page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton2 processors. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores running on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture at a fixed clock speed of 2.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. For networking, it provides a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with no GPUs attached.

The primary differentiator of the im4gn.xlarge is its bundled local high-speed storage, featuring a single 1875 GB NVMe SSD. This local non-volatile volume delivers direct-attached low-latency storage capacity that bypasses network-attached block storage overhead. Benchmark testing indicates balanced data-handling capabilities, evidenced by average performance tiers in PassMark database operations and sustained large-block memory read/write bandwidths of 69.63 GB/sec and 33.78 GB/sec, respectively.

Compute benchmarks reflect the limitations of the power-efficient Neoverse-N1 architecture under raw processing stress. Synthetic compute metrics fall primarily into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 936.0, a multi-core score of 3191.0, and weak scores across multi-core stress-ng, Clang compilation, and decompression tests. Similarly, Redis SET operations reached 4.92 million operations per second, scoring in the lower quartile. The architecture trades peak single-thread execution speed for energy efficiency and continuous storage throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the im4gn.xlarge offers an economical footprint for applications that demand substantial local NVMe storage paired with modest compute requirements. It serves as an effective platform for distributed NoSQL databases, log aggregation nodes, caching layers requiring high-capacity disk persistence, and ETL staging nodes, where IOPS and storage capacity take precedence over raw CPU performance.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized cloud instance built on AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors using the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. Powered by the AWS Nitro System, the instance features 4 dedicated physical vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz, 16.0 GB of memory, and a 6 Gbps baseline network capacity. It includes a dedicated 1875 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering dense storage capacity without the latency of networked volumes. Benchmark results show average performance in PassMark database operations alongside sustained uncached memory throughput, though raw compute metrics in Geekbench and multi-threaded decompression register in lower percentiles. With its dedicated storage-to-compute ratio, the im4gn.xlarge is well tailored for intermediate storage-bound workloads, such as distributed database nodes, real-time log ingestion, search indices, and local transactional file caches where NVMe disk density is the driving infrastructure requirement.
